featured_reviews.name: Prashant “Paddy” Demello
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited the newly renovated Shree Laxmi Vilas Bar in Malad East, and while there are a few things to appreciate, the overall experience ended up being a mixed bag — definitely not beyond 3 stars.

To begin with the positives, the renovation is genuinely impressive. The place looks fresh, modern, and much more inviting compared to most local bars in the area. The interior design is clean, well-lit, and thoughtfully done. The seating layout is comfortable and the ambience gives the feeling of a higher-end local bar. Even the crowd seemed more decent and composed than what you would typically expect in similar neighbourhood bars. This immediately makes the place feel safer and more comfortable, especially if you’re coming with friends.

However, the experience fell apart when it came to service and food, which are two of the most important aspects of any bar or restaurant. The waiter was completely inattentive — barely making eye contact, not checking on the table, and showing no interest in assisting with the order. When we pointed out issues, there was hardly any response.

The worst part was the Chicken Lollipop we ordered. The outer coating was extremely hard — so hard that it was difficult to bite into — but the waiter didn’t seem bothered at all. There was no attempt to replace it, apologise, or even acknowledge the complaint. It felt like the staff was simply not trained or not interested in customer satisfaction. The rest of the food was mediocre at best, definitely not worth the price they charge. For the kind of rates we paid, the quality should have been far better. It felt more like regular bar food but priced as premium.

They do have a smoking room, which is appreciated, but it clearly doesn’t match the new interiors. It looks old, under-maintained, and completely out of sync with the renovated main area. If they’ve taken the effort to upgrade the interior, the smoking room should be improved to the same standard.

Overall, Shree Laxmi Vilas Bar has potential — good ambience, good crowd, and a newly upgraded environment — but the poor service and disappointing food really pull the entire experience down. A place with such nice interiors should ideally offer much better hospitality. For now, it remains an average experience at best.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had an extremely disturbing and disappointing experience at Green Tadka, and it completely destroyed the image I had of this place.

When you choose a restaurant that looks decent and well-maintained, you naturally expect clean, hygienic food and professional standards. You believe that if you’re paying to eat at a “good” restaurant, your food will at least be safe. Unfortunately, that trust was completely broken here.

I ordered a dosa and found a dead mosquito inside it — absolutely disgusting and shocking. No customer should ever have to face something like this. It immediately makes you question what kind of hygiene standards they follow and what else might be happening behind the scenes.

What made things even more concerning is that the dosa wasn’t even prepared in a proper kitchen. It was being made openly in the restaurant area itself, exposed to the environment, customers walking around, and clearly insects as well. Watching food being prepared in such an unhygienic, open manner explains exactly how something like a mosquito could end up inside a dish. It shows a serious lack of food safety practices.

To make matters worse, I had already eaten a dosa from there earlier. Now I’m left wondering whether that one was safe or not, which is honestly disturbing.

The manager,did apologize, but then said something completely illogical — he told me not to pay for the previous dosa I had ordered. Waiving payment doesn’t fix a hygiene disaster. It felt more like an attempt to brush the issue under the carpet than to genuinely resolve it.

The manager, clearly did not know how to handle a serious customer complaint. Instead of responding calmly, professionally, and taking proper responsibility, he seemed confused and unprepared. His way of dealing with the situation felt careless and illogical, as if he was trying to avoid the issue rather than resolve it. Rather than reassuring the customer and offering a clear solution, he gave vague answers and excuses, which made the situation even more frustrating. A manager is supposed to lead, take accountability, and protect the restaurant’s standards — but in this case, there was a complete lack of professionalism and proper complaint handling.

When I asked for the owner’s contact number or email to know him about the situation so I could escalate the matter, I was told, “Owner gaon gaya hai.” No contact details, no proper complaint process, no accountability — just excuses.

A restaurant’s reputation is built on trust. Customers trust that the food they are served is prepared safely and hygienically. Here, not only was that trust broken, but the way the situation was handled afterward showed a complete lack of professionalism and concern for customer health.

I left feeling disgusted, shocked, and extremely disappointed.

This was one of the worst dining experiences I’ve ever had, and I would strongly advise others to think twice before eating here. No one should risk their health at a place that claims to be a quality restaurant but fails at the most basic standards of cleanliness and responsibility.

This is a major hygiene issue and poses a risk to customer health. I request a proper explanation of how such contamination occurred, details of the hygiene measures followed in food preparation, and assurance that corrective action will be taken to prevent this from happening again. I also request to speak with the owner or a senior authority, as the issue was not handled satisfactorily by the manager on duty,Please treat this matter seriously and respond at the earliest with a clear resolution..

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for a satisfying pure veg dining experience in Malad, Classic Pure Veg Restaurant is definitely worth a visit.

We kicked off the meal with a comforting **broccoli almond soup**—creamy, mildly nutty, and a perfect start. The **chef’s special pizza** was loaded with toppings and had a nicely baked crust, while the **paneer shole tikka** stood out with its smoky flavour and well-balanced spices.

The **matka dum biryani** was a highlight—fragrant, well-layered, and served piping hot, making it both comforting and filling.

To end on a sweet note, the **gadbad ice cream** was delightful—loaded with textures, flavours, and just the right amount of indulgence.

Overall, a place that nails both variety and flavour. Great for family dinners or when you want to indulge in a hearty vegetarian feast!

We ordered quite a lot – Paneer Kulcha Masala, Paneer Satay, Paneer Tikka, Veg Biryani, Damy Ban Masala Dosa, Thatti Idli, and Mysore Masala Dosa. Every dish had its own flavor and felt freshly made. featured_reviews.name: Asad Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Having always wanted to visit Lucky Restaurant, the legendary Bandra West institution famous for a Biryani so iconic it is famously loved by actor Salman Khan’s family, I was thrilled to try their brand-new branch in Goregaon East.
We started with the Chicken Manchow Soup, which was served remarkably hot and tasted fantastic with a rich, delicious, masala-based flavor, though a few unblended chunks occasionally disrupted the texture. Unfortunately, the Prawns Chilly starter was a letdown, featuring tiny, chewy prawns and an average sauce that we ultimately couldn't finish.
However, the highly anticipated Chicken Biryani completely redeemed the meal. It was absolutely perfect, boasting a flawless blend of spices, tender meat, and a delicious accompanying raita that made the whole visit worthwhile. We wrapped up with the Apricot Delight dessert, which was spectacularly flavorful and highly recommended.
Across the board, the portions were much larger than expected, justifying the slightly expensive pricing, and the service from the super nice staff was excellent. My only critique is that they should expand their soft drink menu beyond standard Pepsi and Coca-Cola to include options like Campa, Big Cola, and Lahori to better complement their heavy, flavorful dishes.

featured_reviews.name: bhushan bowlekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Paying ₹710 for this oily, pathetic dish is honestly shocking.

Ordered Lollipop Khepsa from Lucky Restaurant today, and honestly, it was one of the worst food experiences I've had.
The dish was drowning in oil. My hands were literally covered with oil while eating, and even my throat got irritated afterward.
When I called the restaurant, instead of taking responsibility, they simply said, "Utna to hota hi hai" and started giving excuses.
This is not Khepsa — it's just oily fried rice loaded with excessive oil. The quality was terrible, the taste was disappointing, and the amount of oil used was ridiculous.
Extremely frustrated and disappointed. If this is the standard of food being served, customers deserve much better. Not recommended at all.

featured_reviews.name: Iqra Memon
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very disappointing experience at Lucky Restaurant. The food was not up to the mark. We ordered Chicken Tikka, but the gravy served did not seem like Chicken Tikka at all. When we brought this to the staff's attention, they agreed to change it and suggested that we try Chicken Matka instead. However, it appeared that they simply reheated the same gravy, added some butter on top, and served it again.
The service was equally disappointing. We requested a tissue refill four separate times, but no one seemed concerned enough to attend to it. The staff appeared inactive and inattentive throughout our visit.
Overall, both the food quality and service fell far below expectations. I hope the management takes customer feedback seriously and works on improving these aspects.

featured_reviews.name: vishal sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently dined at Lucky Restaurant and it turned out to be a delightful culinary experience.

We ordered the half Murg Mussallam, which came with two rich and flavorful gravies – one a vibrant yellow and the other a deep red. The dish was generously topped with juicy tandoori chicken pieces, making it both unique and hearty. Paired with butter garlic naan, the meal was absolutely satisfying and more than enough for two people.

For dessert, we tried the Arabian pudding, which was a real highlight – rich, creamy, and beautifully balanced in flavor. The caramel custard was just as expected – smooth and classic, a comforting end to the meal.

The service was prompt and courteous, and the prices were reasonable for the quality and portion size. A special shoutout to the kitchen for the thoughtful preparation and presentation.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for flavorful Non veg Indian dishes and comforting desserts in a relaxed setting.

featured_reviews.name: minakshi sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
We have been regular customers of Lucky and have always trusted the quality of your food. However, our experience on 3rd January 2026 was extremely disappointing and concerning.

We ordered 1 kg Chicken Biryani, which was delivered hot and consumed immediately. Within two hours, the remaining biryani developed a strong foul smell, and all of us suffered from stomach issues afterward. This clearly indicates a serious lapse in food quality and hygiene, which is unacceptable.

This is the first time we have faced such an issue with Lucky, but it has significantly affected our trust. Serving food that can cause health issues is a serious matter and must be addressed urgently.

I request you to investigate this incident, take strict corrective action, and ensure such negligence does not happen again. I also expect an appropriate response from your side regarding this matter

featured_reviews.name: Ap Consultants
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the best mutton biryani in Mumbai. The mutton pieces are soft and delicate along with a piece of potato which makes the biryani all the more interesting and scrumptious. It's has always been my all time favourite.
When I can't visit the restaurant I order it from Swiggy/Zomato.
Must try for every biryani lover.

featured_reviews.name: Suyash Karangutkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our recent visit to Lucky Biryani turned out to be a delicious journey through rich Mughlai flavours, ending with some comforting desserts that rounded off the meal perfectly.

We ordered the Murg Musallam, and it was easily the highlight of our meal. A whole chicken, richly marinated and cooked in a thick, aromatic gravy made with a blend of spices, nuts, and cream – the dish was indulgent, flavorful, and felt true to its royal roots. The chicken was tender, infused with spices, and the gravy was luscious without being overly heavy. The quantity was more than sufficient for two to three people and extremely filling, making it great value for money.

To go along with it, we had Butter Garlic Naan – soft, perfectly cooked with a generous brush of butter and a strong hit of garlic that paired beautifully with the Musallam.

For dessert, we tried the Arabian Pudding, a milk-based sweet that was delicate and smooth, with hints of cardamom and saffron. It was light and refreshing after the rich main course.

We also had the Caramel Custard, which was classic and well-done – creamy, just the right amount of sweetness, and topped with a golden layer of caramel that melted on the tongue.

Overall, Lucky Biryani delivered a satisfying meal – flavour-packed, generously portioned, and rounded off with nostalgic desserts. A great spot if you’re in the mood for classic Mughlai fare done right.

featured_reviews.name: Bryan Kisten
featured_reviews.review_text:
had a horrible experience at Lucky Restaurant. I have been a loyal customer for over 10 years, but unfortunately, the quality of their service has drastically declined.
During my recent visit, the staff was inattentive and unprofessional. We had to wait an unusually long time just to place our order, and even longer for the food to arrive. When the food finally came, it was not served fresh and did not match the quality and taste that the restaurant was once known for even tho the restaurant was empty
Additionally, the staff seemed disinterested in addressing customer concerns. Basic hospitality and courtesy were missing, which made the overall dining experience extremely disappointing. The restaurant also appeared poorly managed, with delays, lack of coordination among staff, and a noticeable drop in cleanliness standards.
It is very unfortunate to see a place that once maintained such good standards now failing to meet even basic customer expectations. I genuinely hope the management takes customer feedback seriously and works towards improving their service and quality.

featured_reviews.review_text: We were with family and there was no proper waiter to assist us around. Service is not at all good. Even the plates and glasses there were different in sizes and shapes. featured_reviews.name: Arvind Rao
featured_reviews.review_text:
If I had to describe this place in short.. it would be “a place which reminds us that family dinner should best be enjoyed at HOME”

Neither does this place have the common courtesy to take care of senior citizens (especially the ones with jain preference)

Nor does it have the ability to take care of a big family which has children and their dietary preference..

4 out of 5 orders were taken wrongly and the quality and taste of the food was something like I mentioned before “a strict reminder” that family dinners should be actually done at home.

We ordered a fungi pasta (for kids) which we specifically pointed out; a wrong order of normal pasta (totally tasteless) was served to us.

We ordered a jain dish of potato (which was to be served with pocket papad; it was a weird potato dish with a hint of garlic!) and no pocket papad

We ordered for a kofta curry (we specifically asked the waiter if this will be enough for 6 adults and 2 kids) he didn’t utter a word; during serving we see literally 2 koftas with gravy (again tasteless) when we asked the waiter why wouldn’t he suggest something better he brashly said “do hi kofta aata hain”

We specifically asked him to switch the AC on multiple times as we felt suffocated; neither did he bother with listening to us first few times; nor did he do anything about it..

All of this just RUINED our family dinner spirit and mood!

I will not at all recommend this place if you’re planning to have a nice family dinner.. their staff makes you feel “unwanted” and their AC section is more like a sauna bath.

Stay far far away from this place, I’m praying we don’t get food poisoning because our mind feels thoroughly poisoned with this restaurants ambience and service.. they ruined a family get together..

NEVER RETURNING HERE, NOR RECOMMENDING THIS PLACE!

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Sunil Parab
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve been visiting Hotel Sapna for nearly 30 years, and their consistency is truly commendable. Building a strong reputation is difficult, but maintaining it over decades is even more impressive — and Hotel Sapna has done exactly that.

Whenever I’m in Mumbai, this is my go-to place for vegetarian food. The menu offers a huge variety of dishes, and what stands out most is their willingness to customise preparations according to individual preferences and suggestions.

The food quality, taste, and service have remained consistently excellent over the years, making every visit enjoyable. Whether it’s a work meeting, catching up with friends, a family dinner, or a small gathering, Hotel Sapna is always a perfect choice.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for delicious vegetarian food and a reliable dining experience in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Shantanu Dey (Sandy)
featured_reviews.review_text:
I happened to be in Malad with 3 friends and was looking for some breakfast on Swami Vivekananda road. Not familiar with the restaurants in the area we took the advise of a local and reached Sapna Pure Veg.
This is the typical ‘Kamath’ restaurant of Mumbai which serve mostly South Indian fare and some Marathi delights like sabudana vada. However I was pleasantly impressed with what Sapna offers, that included pizza,  bao, Chinese, North Indian, sandwiches etc. We went for dosa, idli-vada-sambhar and sabudanavada. Liked the food. Coffee was not to the mark.
The place is quite spacious with colourful interiors.

Had a really disappointing experience at this restaurant. The service was extremely poor from start to finish. Our order was taken incorrectly, and despite pointing it out, it took forever to fix it. There was an unreasonable delay in serving the food and the overall service was painfully slow.
What made it worse was the attitude of the staff. The waiters were rude, unprofessional and didn’t seem to care at all about customer satisfaction. Instead of being helpful, they came across as arrogant and dismissive.
Definitely not a place I’d recommend. There are far better options out there where customers are actually treated with respect.
